strategies.summary: With higher-timeframe context already set, wait for sell-side liquidity to be swept and reclaimed, then require a strong bullish displacement before targeting opposing buy-side liquidity. Liquidity pools can be equal highs, equal lows or the far side of a consolidation, so the target stays text-only.

timeframes.notes: Fractal concept with no fixed labels: choose the execution chart for the sweep/reaction, and read higher-timeframe context from one or more rungs above it via the contract ladder. The canonical bullish rewrite uses sell-side sweep -> bullish displacement; bearish setups mirror through the catalog mirror table.

glossary.Liquidity pool: A cluster of stops or resting liquidity, such as equal highs/lows or the far side of a consolidation.
glossary.Liquidity run: A breach that keeps going instead of reclaiming the swept side and displacing away from it.

custom_signals.name: pure_sweep
custom_signals.plain_definition: Price trades through a swing low (sell-side liquidity) and the sweeping candle closes back above it (turtle soup).

custom_signals.name: displacement_candle
custom_signals.plain_definition: A strong expansion candle in the trade direction.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: close > open AND body >= K_DISPLACEMENT_BODY_MULT * avg(body[-1], K_DISPLACEMENT_LOOKBACK)

custom_signals.name: displacement_reaction
custom_signals.plain_definition: A strong, immediate move away from a swept level (bullish: after sell-side is swept).

custom_signals.name: failed_rejection
custom_signals.plain_definition: Price sweeps a level but does not displace away from it immediately, drifting instead.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: count(structural_event.kind == liquidity_sweep_low, K_REACTION_WINDOW_CANDLES + 1) > count(structural_event.kind == liquidity_sweep_low, K_REACTION_WINDOW_CANDLES) AND NOT any(custom_signals.displacement_candle, K_REACTION_WINDOW_CANDLES)

sequence: Wait for sell-side liquidity to be swept on the execution chart.
Require the sweeping candle to close back above the swept level.
Enter only after a strong bullish displacement confirms the rejection, targeting opposing buy-side liquidity.

invalidation.text: Price stays above the swept high (or below the swept low) for too long, turning the sweep into a liquidity run.

filters.text: Do not instantly target the opposite side just because one side was swept; a confirmed reaction is mandatory.
Must be traded with higher timeframe context to avoid confusion.

entry_rule.text: Enter long only after the reclaimed sweep produces a clear bullish displacement/reaction.
entry_rule.quote: we need some sort of reaction... because when we get that reaction we can truly Target opposite side

target_rule.text: Target opposing buy-side liquidity such as equal highs or the far side of the consolidation that built the sweep.
target_rule.quote: what is above Price Right Here equal highs... where do we target right there relatively equal highs get taken

presenter_claims.claim: The majority of traders never get past simple support/resistance and trendline patterns, providing liquidity for institutions.

strategies.notes: The presenter teaches a market-mechanics concept rather than a fixed PD-array execution model. A valid sweep needs the registry's pure_sweep reclaim because the engine liquidity_sweep_* signal itself fires on wick or body breaches. The exact higher-timeframe context and the exact opposing target pool remain discretionary.

uncertainties.why: The presenter explains the necessity of a 'reaction' or 'displacement' after the sweep, but does not specify exactly which PD array (FVG, OB, etc.) should be used for the entry execution in this specific lesson.
The presenter insists on higher-timeframe context or a PD array, but does not state one exact measurable detector or a fixed timeframe pair.

confidence.reason: The theoretical framework and targeting rules are extremely clear, but the exact mechanical entry and stop-loss rules are omitted in favor of teaching macro concepts.
